$comment: Print engines quoted inside Axim print-and-apply systems, documented by the
people who make them.
Every URL here was resolved by hand and checked to return 200 — the images, the
product pages and the datasheets. None is constructed from a model number. A
plausible URL that 404s in front of a customer is worse than no link, and the same
rule governs the datasheet citations on the rules.
The Kestrel engines were absent from the first pass because nobody had checked their
pages. Told where to look — "Kestrel has the information on their site too" — so they
are here now on the same terms as the Palisade ones.
'doc' is what a rep would ask for by name; 'docUrl' is where it actually is.
`kind` is what the link should be CALLED. Palisade publishes a spec-sheet PDF;
Kestrel publishes a specifications web page. Labelling both 'datasheet (PDF)'
was reported as a bug on the Axim side and it was the same bug here.
The Corvus 7300 series is photographed in two places and neither is axim.example,
whose 9000 page is marketing copy and icons. The four standard machines share the
studio shot from page 2 of the Corvus brochure — they are one cabinet, with
identical dimensions on the brochure's own table — and the 7340 Prism has its
own from Corvus's product page, where the cabinet is badged so a rep can see which
machine it is.
`imagePdf` extracts from a document at build time and is pinned by page, image
index and expected dimensions: a reissued brochure fails the build rather than
quietly shipping whatever image landed at that position.
